correctness.rationale: For fixed r heavy weights a_i>0 with sum<1, positive diffuse remainder d, max dust weight→0, and common exponential discovery clocks, the dust process converges uniformly in probability to d(1-e^-t) using symmetrization/maximal inequality with error ≤4√(d_N b_N). Heavy clocks remain independent Exp1; positive continuous diffuse drift stabilizes strict crossing despite occasional jump overshoots, yielding T=inf{t:X(t)>θ}. Conditioning on active subset gives survival with STRICT a_A+d(1-e^-t)<θ, including deterministic atom times t_A=-log(1-(θ-a_A)/d), at most 2^r. Binary heavy weights attain this. Poisson optional stopping controls draw count K_N/N versus rescaled physical time in L2 and exponential missing-weight tails ensure all q>0 moments. Independently checked one-heavy masses 1/6,1/6,2/3 and eight distinct atomic sites for r=3. Finite checks do not establish uniform convergence theorem.
